heroIntro: Under Section 126 of the Contract Act 1872 and established Appellate Division precedent, Bangladeshi banks must honour unconditional Bank Guarantees and Letters of Credit strictly according to their terms regardless of underlying contract disputes. Courts grant injunctions restraining encashment only upon clear prima facie proof of egregious fraud or irretrievable injustice.

sections.title: The Autonomy Principle Under Contract Act Section 126
sections.content:
A Bank Guarantee under Section 126 of the Contract Act 1872—like an irrevocable Letter of Credit under ICC UCP 600—constitutes an independent, self-contained contract between the issuing bank and the beneficiary completely separate from the underlying supply or construction agreement. When a contractor, importer, or EPC vendor disputes termination notices or liquidated damages claims with a government agency or foreign buyer, that underlying contract disagreement normally cannot stop the issuing bank from honouring a valid written demand.

Both the High Court Division and the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh consistently protect the commercial certainty of bank commitments in domestic infrastructure tenders and international trade finance. If commercial courts routinely stayed unconditional guarantees whenever a contractor alleged wrongful termination, letters of credit and tender securities issued by Bangladeshi banks would lose international credibility.

Before drafting demand letters or contesting procurement forfeitures, businesses should examine contractual breach principles, review import cargo clearance disputes, and understand general civil injunction criteria.

sections.title: Two Narrow Legal Exceptions: Fraud & Irretrievable Harm
sections.content:
Bangladeshi courts grant temporary injunctions under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 only when the plaintiff establishes either egregious fraud known to the bank or irretrievable injustice making later restitution impossible. Mere assertions of unfair termination, force majeure delays, or arithmetic billing disagreements never cross the legal threshold required to restrain unconditional instruments:

Legal Ground / ScenarioLikelihood of InjunctionKey Evidentiary Burden
Ordinary Underlying Contract DisputeRejected (Autonomy Applies)Recoverable later via money suit or arbitration
Egregious Fraud (Fake Bills/Lading)Granted (High Threshold)Clear documentary proof of forged shipping/inspection docs
Conditional Guarantee Pre-Condition UnmetGranted via Strict TermsDemand omits mandatory engineer certificate or notice
Irretrievable Injustice (Insolvent Foreign Buyer)Exceptional GrantProof beneficiary sits beyond enforceable recovery reach

Equally important, conditional guarantees requiring strict presentation of a defect certificate or expiry timeline can be restrained if the beneficiary's demand letter breaches explicit textual conditions. Where banks wrongfully freeze operating accounts beyond guarantee margins, examine bank account freeze defenses and CIB reporting protection rules.

sections.title: How to Seek an Injunction Against Unlawful Encashment
sections.content:
Because banks typically remit unconditional guarantee funds within twenty-four to forty-eight banking hours of demand presentation, speed and strict documentary precision before the Civil Judge or Joint District Judge are decisive. Follow this litigation workflow immediately upon learning of a fraudulent encashment call:

  1. Serve Immediate Fraud Alert Notice on Issuing Bank: Deliver a formal written notice enclosing documentary proof of forgery, expired guarantee dates, or unmet textual conditions to the bank's Trade Operations Head before remittance clears.
  2. File Declaratory & Permanent Injunction Suit: Institute a civil suit under Sections 42 and 54 of the Specific Relief Act 1877 naming both the beneficiary and the issuing bank as co-defendants in the competent court.
  3. Move Urgent Order XXXIX Ad-Interim Restraint Application: File an affidavit-backed temporary injunction petition under CPC Order XXXIX Rules 1–2 requesting urgent status quo or ad-interim restraint pending show-cause hearing.
  4. Escalate via Civil Revision or Writ Where Appropriate: Where a subordinate court arbitrarily refuses urgent status quo or where a public statutory corporation invokes a guarantee violating public law transparency, pursue Civil Revision or a High Court Writ Petition alongside a formal stay application.

Do not delay filing until after the bank transfers funds; once money is wired abroad or credited to the beneficiary, injunction proceedings become infructuous and convert into slow money recovery suits.

sections.title: Essential Evidence Checklist for Injunction Hearings
sections.content:
Civil judges scrutinize whether fraud pleadings rely on indisputable contemporaneous documents rather than self-serving contractor emails or speculative allegations. Assemble this complete evidentiary bundle prior to the first injunction hearing:

  • Certified copy of the original Bank Guarantee or irrevocable Letter of Credit showing exact expiry date, governing UCP 600 / URDG 758 clauses, and demand conditions.
  • Executed underlying EPC, procurement, or international sales contract together with any written scope amendments and extension approvals.
  • Beneficiary's formal encashment call letter showing exact date of presentation and whether mandatory preconditions were omitted.
  • Hard evidence proving egregious fraud—such as falsified bills of lading, inspection reports repudiated by testing labs, or prior written completion certificates contradicting default claims.
  • Banking correspondence, SWIFT MT799 / MT700 messages, and forensic signature verification records where forgery is alleged.
  • Proof of irretrievable harm, such as beneficiary liquidation proceedings or verified inability to enforce future arbitral awards in the beneficiary's home jurisdiction.

Importers facing customs detention over defective LC shipments should coordinate evidence directly with Customs Appellate Tribunal defense filings.

sections.title: Appellate Division Standards & Strategic Defense
sections.content:
Successfully obtaining or vacating an LC or Bank Guarantee injunction in Bangladesh depends on framing the petition strictly within Appellate Division exceptions rather than relitigating contract merits prematurely. Even when an injunction is refused against an unconditional guarantee, contractors retain full legal authority to recover wrongfully encashed sums plus bank charges and commercial interest through subsequent money suits, Artha Rin counter-claims, or domestic arbitration awards.

Conversely, issuing banks and corporate beneficiaries wrongly blocked by ex-parte subordinate court stay orders can swiftly move to vacate unmeritorious restraints by demonstrating compliance with UCP 600 document rules and availability of post-encashment monetary restitution. faqs.question: Can a Bangladeshi court stop payment under an unconditional Bank Guarantee?
faqs.answer: Only in rare, exceptional cases. Because Bank Guarantees operate independently of underlying commercial contracts under Section 126 of the Contract Act 1872, courts refuse injunctions over ordinary contractual disputes and restrain encashment only upon strict prima facie proof of egregious fraud or irretrievable injustice.

faqs.question: Does fraud in the underlying supply contract justify blocking an LC payment?
faqs.answer: Under ICC UCP 600 and Appellate Division precedent, minor quality defects or pricing disputes do not stop Letter of Credit payment. However, proven documentary fraud—such as forged bills of lading, non-existent cargo shipments, or counterfeit inspection certificates brought to the bank's clear notice before negotiation—justifies judicial restraint.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a conditional and unconditional bank guarantee?
faqs.answer: An unconditional demand guarantee requires the issuing bank to pay immediately upon receiving a simple written claim stating default, without investigating actual breach. A conditional guarantee requires the beneficiary to satisfy specified preconditions—like attaching a third-party engineer's certificate—giving courts clear authority to restrain defective demands.

faqs.question: Which court handles urgent injunctions against bank guarantee encashment?
faqs.answer: An aggrieved applicant files a declaratory and permanent injunction suit paired with an Order XXXIX temporary injunction petition in the Civil Judge or Joint District Judge Court holding territorial jurisdiction over the issuing bank branch, with urgent revision or writ escalation available before the High Court Division.

faqs.question: If the court refuses an injunction and the bank pays, is the money lost forever?
faqs.answer: No. Bank Guarantee encashment determines interim possession of money, not final contractual liability. The contractor or importer can still pursue a full civil recovery suit or commercial arbitration claim to recover wrongfully called guarantee proceeds together with bank margin costs and statutory damages if breach was unjustified.
